sources.entry: ZOC Terminal - Terminal emulator which supports SSH, telnet, connections and other protocols.

summary.name: ZOC Terminal
summary.one_liner: ZOC Terminal is a tabbed SSH client and terminal emulator for Windows and macOS with a host directory, terminal emulations and scripting.
use_cases: Connecting to remote Linux or Unix servers over SSH
Managing many servers from a saved host directory
Connecting through a corporate SOCKS or HTTP proxy
Running remote GUI programs over X11 forwarding
Connecting to older servers that need legacy ciphers
Authenticating with smart cards or SSH keys
summary.what_it_does: The page describes ZOC Terminal as an SSH client with a modern tabbed interface, a host directory, terminal emulations and scripting. It supports password, public-key (RSA, DSA, ECDSA, ED25519) and keyboard-interactive authentication, plus hardware smart card keys. It supports a broad range of SSH ciphers, from aes256-ctr down to older ones such as aes256-cbc and arcfour. Connections can go through SOCKS-4, SOCKS-5, HTTP proxies and SSH jump servers, and it offers dynamic port forwarding, agent forwarding and X11 forwarding. The page also mentions telnet and other protocols via the awesome-mac listing.
notable: Dynamic port forwarding with a listening port that accepts any destination
Supports SOCKS-4, SOCKS-5, HTTP proxies and SSH jump servers
Broad cipher support including legacy ciphers for older servers
SSH agent forwarding and X11 forwarding
caveats: Older ciphers such as aes256-cbc and arcfour are included mainly for compatibility with old servers and may be less secure
Pricing and licensing are not stated on the page
